children: none, because the seam is bounded to one file and one already-existing proof: the change is a payload field plus two constructor arguments in cairn/devices/aider_shim/driver.py, and its teeth grow in cairn/devices/aider_shim/proofs/test_driver.py. The probe named in the watch is not a child — it is this node's own WATCHME obligation, armed before the crossing at the berth the spec names.

questions.a: AFTER THIS CHANGE THE TEST RUNS TWICE ON A DRIVE THAT REACHES AN EDIT, and only one of them is evidence: aider's, inside the loop, is the apprentice's feedback signal; the parent's run_test is the record's authority and is what DriveResult.test carries. A reader finding two invocations and assuming redundancy would delete the wrong one. This distinction belongs in the code at the seam, not only here.

THE DRIVER'S EXISTING COMMENT IS NOT CONTRADICTED. 'WE run the test, so its result is ours to carry' protects whose result the RECORD carries — it exists so DriveResult.test is not scraped out of aider's chat. It does not protect aider's ignorance of the test; that was a consequence of the setting rather than its purpose, and the record's authority never moves.

A CALLABLE test_cmd IS THE DESIGN THAT WOULD HAVE KEPT THE COMMENT LITERALLY TRUE AND IT IS IMPOSSIBLE. commands.cmd_test accepts one (commands.py:1002-1010), but test_cmd is also concatenated into the system prompt unguarded at base_coder.py:1169, so a callable raises `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'function' and 'str'` on every message format. Measured in the shim's own venv, both variants, before this cast. Recorded so the next reader does not re-derive it from the call site, where the two designs look equally available.

THE PARENT CANNOT OWN THE LOOP WITHOUT DISCARDING THE CONVERSATION. run_in_venv is a one-shot subprocess and a Coder does not survive the process boundary, so a parent-side retry would re-pay full context and lose the model's own reasoning between attempts — the expensive shape AND the one least likely to converge.

THE CONVERGENCE IS MEASURED, NOT ARGUED. 2026-08-18T06:23:52Z, qwen3-coder:30b on hex, a scratch repo whose check.py demands the literal token SENTINEL-4417 inside add.__doc__ — a requirement deliberately absent from the 255-char brief and absent from calc.py's pre-drive bytes. Attempt 1 wrote `return a + b` and failed; aider ran the test itself; the apprentice's second reply opens "I need to add a docstring to the `add` function that contains the exact token \"SENTINEL-4417\"". That token existed in exactly ONE place the model could have read it — the assertion message — reachable only through aider's own in-process run. calc.py went 28 -> 56 bytes and the parent's run_test returned 0. A live fire that happened to PASS on attempt 1 would have measured nothing about this mechanism; the failure had to be manufactured, and that is the design of the fixture, not an accident of it.

A CACHE HIT IS NOT A SECOND OPINION, and the population had already had determinism misread off one. The first successful drive recorded num_reflections 1 with BOTH asks served from the fence's cache (prompt_eval_counts [null, null]); the probe scored it live_reflected_asks 0 and refused to count it. Changing the sentinel forced a miss and the re-fire records [null, 2452]. The probe was right and the drive record was the thing that looked complete.

CORRECTED 2026-08-18T06:40Z, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE POINT: THE ERROR NAMES THE WRONG CAUSE, AND SO DID I. The first live fire died `HostUnmetered ... response carried ['created_at','done','message','model']`, and this entry originally explained it as a client timeout — host.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT 120.0s against a measured 131.5s cold load of qwen3-coder:30b at num_ctx 81920. THAT IS FALSE. It was inferred from two measurements taken apart (a HostUnmetered with a 4-key body; a 131.5s cold load) and never from one run that produced both. Run tonight against hex, it does not survive: unload the model (keep_alive 0, ps confirms empty), fire the identical chat request four times, and every one returns HTTP 200 carrying `{"model":"","created_at":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z","message":{"role":"","content":""},"done":false}` — 96 bytes — at 14.2s, 0.1s, 0.1s, 0.1s. No timeout is involved at any point; the transport never raised, and 0.1s is three orders of magnitude inside the 120s bound. n=6 tonight (2 more from an idle-evicted model, same shape). Given time to finish loading, the identical request succeeds: six consecutive successes at 0.2-8.9s across num_ctx 8192 / 32768 / 81920, so num_ctx is not the discriminator either. WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: while ollama is bringing the model up, /api/chat answers non-streaming requests with a NON-FINAL frame — `done: false`, empty content, zero-value model and timestamp — and host.py's chat branch passes it, because its shape check asks only that `message` be a dict with a str `content`, and "" is one. metered_cost then refuses, and its refusal talks about counters. The counters are missing because nothing was evaluated; nothing was evaluated because the answer was never final. THE FIX IS ONE PREDICATE AND IT IS CHEAPER THAN THE MISDIAGNOSIS: a non-streaming response with `done` false is the host saying "not yet", and it should be refused by that name, before the meter is ever asked. Ticket owed against inference_domain. THE 131.5s FIGURE STANDS as a measurement — it is a successful cold load-and-answer at num_ctx 81920, and it retires the "~18s cold load" folklore in host.py's own validated_messages docstring (measured 2026-08-16, at whatever num_ctx that reading used, which the docstring does not say).

A PARENT-PROCESS MONKEYPATCH IS INVISIBLE TO THE ASK. drive_brief calls run_in_venv, which is `subprocess.run([python(), "-c", source])` — the ask happens in a child. The only injection that reaches it is the `seams` payload field, resolved by driver._seam, which accepts "/abs/file.py:attr" as well as "module.path:attr". Every wire-level measurement in this voyage went through a seam file for that reason.

CRITERION 1'S BERTHED INSTRUMENT WAS NOT RUNNABLE AS WRITTEN — it says to read the second ask's prompt off fence.SeenLog, and SeenLog.record stores ask_chars, never the payload, deliberately, so the ask log cannot accumulate model text. That is a finding about the validate leg, not a lapse of the build: the criterion was answered by two substitutes (the transcribing seam's sidecar, and the response_tail naming the token) and the verdict says so rather than claiming the named instrument ran.

THE CHART'S OWN SCORE, MEASURED RATHER THAN JUDGED (/sail step 9). 172 tool calls between the validate berth printing (2026-08-18T05:52:53Z) and this close, counted off the session transcript rather than estimated — all 172 Bash, this session running bypass-permissions where Bash does the reading and the editing too. A floor, since the closing calls land after the count. Read downward: a good packet is one you barely have to go looking behind, and much of this 172 is a single live fire that had to be diagnosed at the wire before it would run at all. THE NAMED FALSIFICATIONS, second layer, because a score says the packet was thin and never says which field was. (1) SURVEY never listed host.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT, and it is what killed the first live fire — 120.0s against a measured 131.5s cold load of qwen3-coder:30b at num_ctx 81920. The survey inventoried the driver's own surfaces and the fence's, and stopped at the device boundary; the bound that decided whether the voyage could be measured at all sat one component out, in inference_domain. (2) SURVEY never listed that fence.SeenLog.record stores ask_chars and never the prompt — deliberate, so the ask log cannot accumulate model payloads — and VALIDATE then wrote criterion 1's instrument as 'read the second ask's prompt off fence.SeenLog'. The criterion was unrunnable as written; the finding belongs to the survey leg that did not inventory the record's shape and to the validate leg that specified against the un-inventoried shape. (3) The COUNSEL WALKS FIRED OUT OF ORDER at decompose and hypothesize — the tree stratum was consulted after the packet was assembled rather than before, which is the one ordering the brick's own text makes load-bearing ('walk before you split', 'walk before you reason'). It cost nothing measurable here and is recorded because an unrecorded ordering slip is how the stratum boundary stops being measurable. Nothing counts these calls and nothing delivers this finding; it is a hand's act today (ticket the-builds-tool-calls-are-evidence-about-the-chart).

workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> FIXME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(reflection_earns_its_ask) -> [PROVED]

watchme.trigger: every drive recorded to ~/.cairn/devices/aider_shim/0/drives.jsonl — the driver's own record write is the event that already fires, and nothing polls. The probe reads the row's num_reflections against its asks and its test outcome, so a drive that never reflected is a data point too rather than a gap.
watchme.enough: when five drives carrying num_reflections >= 1 have been recorded AND their applied-and-passing rate has a consistent relationship to the unreflected baseline drawn from the same file. Stop early and loudly on either falsifying observation: a reflected drive that ends WORSE than its first attempt left it — the applied-and-self-cancelling state the edit-survival probe's vocabulary has no word for, and the one this loop could actively manufacture by giving a copying apprentice more turns to copy; or a drive whose second ask does not carry the test's failure text, which means the mechanism reports firing while feeding the apprentice nothing.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier: per drive, num_reflections, the ask count and each ask's prompt_eval_count (a reflected ask that is a cache hit is not a second opinion), whether the second ask's payload contains the test's failure text, the test outcome of the drive as recorded, and the survival disposition of the files it touched
watchme.nexus: the hypothesize tree — the same one aider_shim_offload_yield and aider_shim_edit_survival deposit to, deliberately, so the three watches answer their different questions over ONE drives.jsonl population rather than each demanding its own five real tickets
watchme.consumer: Akien at triage, for whom this is the offload-more vs pull-back decision and specifically the cost half of it — reflection multiplies asks against a metered host, so 'it helps' and 'it helps enough' are different answers and only he settles the second; and CC, who is the party that would otherwise read num_reflections as convergence, which is the exact misreading that bore this ticket
